text:
leah: FYI escalation from CorpX — they see streaming responses cut off after ~70-90s idle, then the client reconnects and sometimes gets only a partial chunk. Billing spike from repeated reconnects. Customer using Cloudflare in front of an ALB (HTTP/2 to CF, HTTP/1.1 to origin).

leah: Repro steps they provided: curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.corpx.example/v1/stream?session=abc' then wait ~90s idle, next event truncated or connection FIN. They see 200 then partial data.

dario: thanks — do we have the X-Request-ID from the failed runs? need the exact request path + edge headers. also what ALB idle timeout is set to on their account?

leah: Provided headers: X-Request-ID: req-0a1b2c3d, CF-Connecting-IP: 203.0.113.12, Via: 1.1 cloudflare. ALB idle timeout reported as 60s in their infra console (they thought default was 60).

jia: interesting. CF default idle to origin is 100s? but ALB 60s could close before CF does h2->h1 connection keepalive dance. Also HTTP/2 h2 connection windowing can buffer. Do they have cloudflare workers / spectrum?

leah: no workers. Cloudflare standard proxy + WAF on. They also said they recently enabled HTTP/2 on ALB (via listener config) to support h2->h1 translation.

mike: quick sanity: ask them to run a raw TCP capture (tcpdump) on the origin host during repro and save pcap. We need to see who sends FIN first and whether ALB is half-closing. Suggest filter: 'tcp and (host 1.2.3.4) and (port 443)'. Also capture conn state from ALB logs.

natalie: possible proxied buffering: nginx/CF/ALB combos often coalesce chunks and delay sending until buffer fills or after idle probes. For nginx origin people often set 'proxy_buffering off;' or send SSE comment heartbeats ':\n' every 15s to keep proxies from considering connection idle. CF can aggregate small writes into bigger ones if it thinks the connection is idle.

leah: CorpX said they attempted sending a 1-byte keepalive every 20s from app, but still saw truncated chunk boundary where last event ended mid-line. They included a sample server log snippet: \n```\n[2026-02-14T15:20:12Z] INFO stream sent chunk id=239 len=512\n[2026-02-14T15:21:35Z] WARN connection idle -> reset by peer (RST) req=req-0a1b2c3d\n[2026-02-14T15:21:35Z] ERROR write failed: broken pipe\n```\n
jia: that RST implies the downstream (ALB/CF) closed. If ALB's idle timeout is 60s and their keepalive 20s, it shouldn't. But note: ALB idle is time between requests on the connection; for streaming, if there's no data at TCP level it may still close if health checks/nat mapping expire. Also Cloudflare has separate idle heuristics for proxied SSE.

dario: does their ALB have HTTP/2 enabled on the listener? if so, check the ALB->target protocol: if ALB speaks h2 to client and h1 to origin, there are head-of-line interactions. Could be ALB buffering until stream ends or until it receives a window update. Recommend reproducing with ALB listener set to HTTP/1.1 client->ALB (disable h2) to see if problem changes.

leah: Customer can toggle that, will try. Meanwhile we suggested a short repro they can run from their infra to simulate: \n```\n# simple SSE server (node) to reproduce keepalive behavior\nconst http = require('http');\nhttp.createServer((req, res) => {\n  res.writeHead(200, {\n    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',\n    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',\n    'Connection': 'keep-alive',\n  });\n  res.write('id: 1\n');\n  res.write('data: hello\n\n');\n  // idle > 60s then send final event\n  setTimeout(() => {\n    res.write('id: 2\\ndata: final\\n\\n');\n    res.end();\n  }, 90000);\n}).listen(3000);\n```\nThen curl with: curl -v -N http://origin:3000/ | sed -n '1,40p'

mike: good. Also ask them to check the target group deregistration/connection-draining settings and NLB vs ALB choice. NLB preserves TCP semantics better for long-lived streams. If they can test switching to NLB (TCP passthrough) and see if the issue disappears it points at ALB/CF HTTP layer buffering/timeouts.

natalie: another quick header they can try from origin: 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' (nginx), 'Cache-Control: no-transform', and SSE heartbeat line starting with ':' e.g. ': ping\n\n' every 10s. For Cloudflare specifically, disable HTTP/2 between CF and ALB? CF to origin is http/1.1 typically. If any intermediate edge terminates TLS, check TLS session resume settings; some TLS session resume issues cause midstream teardown when CF reuses sessions.

leah: customer also attached ALB access log showing the final status code 200 with "received_bytes=... sent_bytes=..." then an immediate connection close. I asked for ENI level logs.

jia: while they gather pcaps, we should provide quick mitigations: 1) Increase ALB idle timeout > 300s (if acceptable) 2) Switch ALB listener to HTTP/1.1 for client and origin path where possible 3) Add SSE heartbeat (':' comment) every 15s 4) Set origin headers to disable buffering (X-Accel-Buffering: no / Cache-Control: no-transform) 5) If feasible, test NLB/TCP passthrough to bypass HTTP layer.

dario: I'll open a low-priority internal investigation ticket to check if we've seen similar with Cloudflare+ALB+SSE in the last 90d. If we find patterns, we should add a KB entry.

leah: CorpX will run the node repro behind their stack and share tcpdump + ALB logs. I'll paste results here when available.

ops-bot: Created escalation INC-2026-143 for thread req-0a1b2c3d and notified oncall. :rotating_light:

mike: one more ask — get a 'raw' response captured by curl with --raw and --no-buffer and save to file. If partial chunk ends mid-event, send me that file. It will show whether a CRLF boundary was lost or if the origin sent partial payload.

leah: will follow up. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
